original_text:
The ONLY AWS Data Engineering roadmap I suggest if you are looking to switch in 2025.

🚀 AWS Data Engineer Roadmap — Step by Step 🛠️
A practical roadmap to go from basics to cloud-native pipelines:

🔹 Level 1: Foundations
 1. SQL – Master joins, windows, CTEs, tuning.
 2. Python – Automate ETL, handle files, use boto3.
 3. Data Modeling – OLTP vs OLAP, star/snowflake schemas.

🔹 Level 2: AWS Core
 4. S3 – Buckets, lifecycle, versioning, partitions.
 5. IAM – Roles, policies, least privilege.
 6. EC2 & VPC – Basic compute & network setup.

🔹 Level 3: ETL & Pipelines
 7. Glue – Spark jobs, crawlers, catalog.
 8. Lambda – Event-driven mini ETLs.
 9. Step Functions – Workflow orchestration.
 10. Kinesis – Real-time streaming pipelines.

🔹 Level 4: Storage & Querying
 11. Redshift – DWH concepts, COPY, Serverless.
 12. RDS/Aurora – Managed SQL DBs.
 13. Athena – Query S3 with SQL + Glue Catalog.

🔹 Level 5: Orchestration & Monitoring
 14. Airflow (MWAA) – Build DAGs with AWS operators.
 15. CloudWatch – Logs, alerts, metrics.
 16. CloudTrail – Audit and trace user activity.

🔹 Level 6: Security & Governance
 17. Encryption/KMS – Secure S3, Redshift, Athena.
 18. Lake Formation – Row/column-level access control.

🔹 Level 7: IaC
 19. Terraform/CloudFormation – Infra as code for repeatable pipelines.

🔹 Level 8: Advanced
 20. DataOps – CI/CD for ETL jobs.
 21. ML Integration – Preprocess data for SageMaker.
 22. Cost Optimization – Monitor & optimize AWS usage.

🔹 Final Step: Projects
 23. Build:
• S3 → Glue → Redshift (Batch)
• Lambda → Kinesis → Redshift (Streaming)
• Athena + QuickSight dashboard
• Airflow DAGs for Glue pipelines
• IaC-based full pipeline

⸻


#AWS #DataEngineering #CloudComputing #Glue #Redshift #Airflow #Kinesis #BigData #CareerRoadmap #SQL #Pyspark #Techinterviews

If you've read so far, do LIKE and RESHARE the post👍

It is a high-level learning outline and does not provide implementation instructions.
